what_is_included_vs_extra.point: At Alert Labs the subscription buys analytics, alerts, dashboards, automated reports, firmware updates and seven-day chat support; it is explicitly not a cellular fee, hub hardware is separate, and onboarding, training and a dedicated customer success manager are support levels to ask about at quote time

LeakSense bundles hardware and installation into the per-unit fee, but free installation only applies to accessible copper or PEX without pipe rerouting; remote valve control, shutoff valves and tenant billing are gated to higher tiers, and the alert channel listed on every tier is email
YouTilitics charges setup separately ($349) and then a platform fee plus per-device fee, so cost scales with sensor count rather than building count; API/webhooks and unlimited users are included

Parker Plumbing bundles hub, sensors, wiring, startup and monthly reports into the monthly fee but prices installation separately after a site visit, and boiler testing is an add-on; alert review and a 24-hour consultation are included

Moen's subscription adds a continuous limited warranty, dedicated support, a 10% moen.com discount and up to $5,000 in insurance deductible coverage; installation is by independent third-party licensed plumbers that Moen does not supervise, is available only in select regions, and is not part of the monthly fee

Leak Shield separates equipment, licensed plumbing, licensed electrical and programming into line items, then bills monitoring annually; live-agent verification, daily plumbing check-ups and plumber dispatch are part of the monthly fee

Monnit's free tier covers basic configuration and email alerts with up to 100 sensors, but SMS alerts and voice calls cost extra, and Premiere (starting @ $45/yr) is what unlocks API access and automated reporting

Inference: Symmons' $30/sensor/month buys a dedicated cellular network, battery backup and enterprise support, and the cellular radio path is a plausible reason it prices above Wi-Fi point sensors that rely on the buyer's own network. Reasoning: the vendor page lists a dedicated cellular network as a differentiator from residential Wi-Fi detectors, which removes the building's network from the alert path, and cellular data is a recurring cost the vendor carries.

Phyn includes pre-freeze warnings and multi-property monitoring (up to 6 properties) with no subscription, but there is no property-management or work-order integration published, unions and adapters are sold separately, and installation is the buyer's own plumber

FireAvert prices each device at MSRP with bulk pricing on request and charges monitoring separately at $60/year, so the platform fee is nearly trivial next to hardware; installation is either FireAvert's team or the property's own staff

buyer_complaints.complaint: Flo by Moen users report false 'fast flow' and micro-leak alerts during ordinary use (showers, irrigation, several fixtures), sometimes followed by an unwanted shutoff, plus app/connectivity frustration
Moen is transitioning users to a new app, and its FAQ says the old app's remote-control features stop working after November 1, 2026 - a reminder that app-dependent systems can change under the buyer
A property-management discussion describes flow-monitor alerts triggered by residents turning water on and off, generating unnecessary emergency maintenance callouts

YoLink users report sensors going offline together (attributed by support to a cloud issue) and, in one case, offline sensors triggering false leak sirens - cheap sensors still need health monitoring and alert-rule testing

A reviewer notes the YoLink leak sensor it covered has no audible alarm of its own, so detection depends on the hub, app and cloud path; YoLink's current Water Leak Sensor 4 listing does say the sensor has a built-in sounder when enabled, so this applies to the older unit reviewed
SimpliSafe states it will not request dispatch of emergency services for water alarms - a monitored plan gets an automated call, not a response, which is a real gap for unoccupied commercial space

Inference: buyers looking at commercial flow-monitoring vendors cannot see a price without a sales conversation - Alert Labs' cost page explains cost drivers and ends at 'request a quote' - which pushes small buyers toward published-price DIY hardware. Reasoning: the page names building count, sensor mix and support level as price drivers but publishes no rate card.

price_ranges.low_cost_self_serve: $19.99-$105 one-time per sensor, or $579.99 for a whole-home shutoff device, plus $0-$60/year for software or monitoring (YoLink Water Leak Sensor 4 $19.99, Hub $23.59 sale/$29.99 list, starter kit $58.99 sale/$75.98 list; FireAvert Leak Detector $40 MSRP, Temp/Humidity $50, Toilet Auto Shutoff $249, Auto Water Shutoff $330, PRO Monitoring $60/year; Monnit sensor $105 with iMonnit Basic Always Free or Premiere from $45/yr; SimpliSafe Water Sensor $19.99 with plans from 33¢/day self monitoring to 76¢/day Standard, billed per household system not per sensor; Phyn Protect $579.99 with no subscription - third-party corroborated)
price_ranges.mid_market: $5-$30 per unit, device or sensor per month, usually with hardware and installation bundled (LeakSense $6-$14/unit/mo; YouTilitics $20/month platform plus $5/device/month with $349 setup; SmartRent $18/unit/mo 2024 promotional bundle; Symmons $30/sensor/month)
price_ranges.full_service_or_custom: $99-$399 per building per month for staffed or installer-led monitoring, with $349-$1,616 of setup/installation in front of it; buyer-reported capital for a 100-unit/500-sensor building was about $10,000-$12,000 with roughly $2/sensor/month (Parker Plumbing $149-$399/mo plus installation; Leak Shield $99/month ($1,188 billed annually) plus $1,616 typical equipment and install; YouTilitics $349 setup; Habitat Magazine-reported $10,000-$12,000 capital and about $2/sensor/month, 2023)
derived_from: WaterSignal (third-party, undated, not used in the arithmetic)
Alert Labs (no published price, so no number used)
price_ranges.inference_note: Inference, not a computed average: each range is the lowest and highest published figure I could open in that tier, with the vendor named so a reader can re-check it. Low-cost uses only one-time hardware and annual software prices from vendor pages (YoLink, FireAvert, Monnit, SimpliSafe, Phyn). Mid-market uses per-unit, per-device or per-sensor monthly subscriptions from vendor pricing pages (LeakSense, YouTilitics, SmartRent promo, Symmons) and therefore starts at $5 rather than $4. Full-service mixes flat monthly vendor plans (Parker, Leak Shield) with one buyer-reported capital figure from Habitat Magazine (2023), which is much larger than a 5-200 staff local business, so the upper bound is soft. Alert Labs and WaterSignal publish no current price and are named but contribute no number; no figure was estimated for them. Third-party figures are labeled as such and not treated as list prices.

implications_for_consultancy: Inference: the realistic competitive set is the installer-led monthly tier ($149-$399/building/month plus installation), not DIY sensors. Reasoning: Parker bundles hub, sensors, wiring, monthly reports and startup for $149-$399, and Leak Shield charges $99/month with a $1,616 install, so a local firm quoting in that band is pricing against an established, published alternative rather than against a $19.99 sensor.

Inference: setup fees of $349-$1,616 are already normalized in this market. Reasoning: YouTilitics charges $349 for gateway setup and onboarding, Leak Shield itemizes $1,616 for a single valve-plus-two-sensors install, and Parker prices installation separately per property. A $500-$1,500 integration/setup fee for a 20-60 point building sits inside the observed range and should be itemized (hardware, labour, programming) the way Leak Shield does it.

Inference: price monitoring per monitored point with a platform floor, not per building. Reasoning: the published commercial plans that show numbers are per unit, per device or per sensor ($5-$30: YouTilitics $5/device, LeakSense $6-$14/unit, SmartRent $18/unit, Symmons $30/sensor), and small commercial buildings around Middlesex County will have 10-60 points; a $150-$300/month floor plus $3-$8 per point maps onto prices buyers already see and protects margin as sensor counts grow.

Inference: hardware markup is not defensible, service is. Reasoning: sensor prices are public and low (YoLink $19.99, FireAvert $40, Monnit $105, SimpliSafe $19.99), so pass hardware through near cost and earn on installation labour, programming, integration and the monthly retainer. Leak Shield's own breakdown (valve $619, sensors $198, plumbing $300, electrical $300, programming $199) is a template for transparent line items.

Inference: the defensible premium is response and integration, not detection. Reasoning: SimpliSafe explicitly will not dispatch for water alarms, YoLink users report cloud-related sensor dropouts, and Flo owners report false alerts and unwanted shutoffs. A retainer that includes alert triage, after-hours escalation to a named person, sensor-health checks, quarterly testing and tuning, plus work-order/PM-system integration, answers the documented complaints and justifies $250-$500/month for a 20-50 point building.

Inference: boiler and freeze coverage is the under-priced wedge for New Jersey. Reasoning: only Parker and FireAvert publish hardware that addresses boiler/heating and freeze risk in this set (Parker lists heating-system monitoring as a plan feature and boiler testing as an add-on without a price; FireAvert sells a $50 temp/humidity sensor), while consumer devices such as Phyn offer only pre-freeze warnings. A combined leak + low-temperature + boiler-room offering aimed at 5-200 staff owners of older Milltown-area buildings is priced against less direct competition than pure leak detection.

Inference: avoid 36-month commitments. Reasoning: Moen's Leak Protection Service requires an initial 36-month term with a cancellation fee of 50% of remaining payments, while LeakSense, YouTilitics and FireAvert are monthly or annual. Offering month-to-month with a discounted annual option is a cheap differentiator for a small local firm and lowers the buyer's approval hurdle.

Inference: sell against the claim, not the subscription. Reasoning: FireAvert cites a national average of about $11,500 per water claim and up to $22,000 in its own portfolio; an annual $3,000-$6,000 retainer is a fraction of one claim, so proposals should lead with the buyer's deductible and insurance-renewal exposure rather than per-sensor price comparisons against YoLink.

Inference: buyers will compare against free-software products, so never sell software access alone. Reasoning: Monnit's Basic tier is 'Always Free' and Phyn states no subscription is required; the paid value has to be installation, commissioning, escalation and reporting, which is what Parker and Leak Shield actually charge for.
caveats: All prices retrieved 2026-11-12 unless a source is dated. Historic or promotional figures are labeled with their year.

Several vendor storefronts render prices with script. YoLink's hub, starter kit and Sensor 4 prices were read off the product pages directly in this revision; Moen's $17.99/month and $49.99 activation came from a search rendering of the Moen product URL because the page text carries the terms but not the figures; Phyn's product page showed no readable price at all, so its $579.99 is a third-party figure attributed to the manufacturer.

Phyn's $579.99 comes from a third-party product profile that says the manufacturer lists that direct price; it is not a figure I could read on phyn.com. An older $699.99 comparison that appeared in an earlier draft has been removed because no openable page showed it.

The YoLink starter kit ($58.99 sale / $75.98 list) is a hub plus four Water Leak Sensor 1 units; the $19.99 per-sensor price is for the different Water Leak Sensor 4, so the two are not interchangeable in comparisons.
Alert Labs publishes no list price of any kind; only an annual subscription per sensor is described. No subscription rate or hardware price is stated here because none could be opened.
WaterSignal's $50/building/month comes from an undated WaterWorld trade article, not from WaterSignal's current price list; WaterSignal and Alert Labs publish no current prices.
SmartRent's $18/unit/month is a 2024 promotional package price from a vendor social post that bundles two leak sensors with a deadbolt, hub and software - it is not a leak-monitoring list price.

SimpliSafe's plans are published per day and billed per household system, not per sensor. The '76¢/day' figure is reproduced exactly; the monthly equivalent shown is arithmetic (76¢ × 365 ÷ 12), not a SimpliSafe price.

No New Jersey or Middlesex County provider with a published monitoring price was found. FSC Leak Detection is New Jersey-based and advertises commercial leak monitoring but publishes no prices; Parker Plumbing serves the Hudson Valley in New York and was used as the nearest published installer-led comparison.
Buyer-reported totals (Habitat, Phantom H2O) are reported, not verified invoices, and cover multifamily buildings much larger than a typical 5-200 staff local business.
Prices exclude sales tax, permits, electrician work outside the quoted scope, and any building Wi-Fi or network upgrades.
Multi-year discounts and volume tiers exist (FireAvert bulk pricing, Leak Shield volume pricing, LeakSense enterprise) but are not published, so they are not reflected in the ranges.
data_gaps: ProSentry (LoRaWAN building monitoring) is dropped from the offerings: its FAQ page contains no prices, and the per-tenant service fee plus per-sensor hardware cost that appeared in an earlier draft could not be corroborated by an independent search or by any prosentry.com page I could open, so no ProSentry figure is used anywhere in this brief.
No published Alert Labs list price for Flowie O, Floodie, Shuttie, Sensor Relay or the AlertAQ subscription, and no public cancellation or refund terms.

A 2021 reseller article (water-controls.com) describes Alert Labs billing as 'a flat fee per sensor / annum' but gives no number and may quote Canadian dollars, so no Alert Labs subscription rate is stated here.

Moen's Flo device is now sold as an enhanced bundle, and the bundle price is rendered by script and could not be read; no Moen device price is used. Moen also publishes no installation rate - installation is quoted by its independent plumber network, and the $49.99 activation fee could only be seen through a search rendering.

A Habitat Magazine podcast episode about one NYC co-op's leak-monitoring rollout was described in a search-indexed summary as about $85,000 upfront for roughly 1,200 sensors plus about $17,000/year, but the podcast page shows only show notes with no figures or transcript, so the number is not used.

The Mercy Housing (Decatur Place, 106 units) case study figures - about $43,000 of sensors, $23,000 grant-funded, first-year savings about $11,606 - appear only in search renderings of the DOE Better Buildings print page, which failed to fetch, so they are not used here.
No openable trade article stating roughly $49 per toilet plus a gateway and an annual monitoring fee was found; that figure has been removed.
No published WaterSignal current price, contract term or statement of what the monitoring fee includes.
Kontrol Technologies publishes no pricing for its water leak detection and monitoring.
ADT's water and temperature sensor has no public per-sensor price, and its PowerG water sensor requires a technician visit with no published installation fee.
No New Jersey-specific published monitoring prices or invoices were found for leak, freeze or boiler monitoring; a local quote survey would be needed to confirm Middlesex County rates.
Boiler-specific monitoring is rarely priced as its own line item; Parker treats heating-system monitoring as part of a plan and boiler testing as an add-on without a price.
No public data on multi-year contract discounts, price escalation at renewal, or sensor replacement/battery costs inside monitoring plans.
